Historical adjacent gaps are tᵢ−tᵢ₋₁; pairwise intervals are |tᵢ−tⱼ|; recommendation-time lag is t_request−t_last. TiSASRec encodes clipped, discretized pairwise intervals in attention keys/values alongside absolute item positions, normalizing by each user’s smallest nonzero gap. It needs historical timestamps, not the next item’s timestamp. TLSRec uses historical gaps to segment sessions, then embeds recommendation-time lag—ceil(lag/minimum gap), capped at C—to gate long-term versus short-term preference dimensionwise. These are distinct temporal signals. [TiSASRec](https://jiachengli1995.github.io/files/wsdm20.pdf), [TLSRec](https://yneversky.github.io/Papers/cikm22.pdf).

TiSASRec compares position-only SASRec, interval-only TiSASRec-R, and their combination: combined encoding wins across all six datasets; interval-only does not consistently beat order-only, partly because tied timestamps erase temporal distinctions. Timestamp-scaling and interval-cap experiments provide additional evidence. TLSRec removes short-/long-term attention, replaces multi-head attention, and replaces its time gate with averaging or attention; full TLSRec performs best. However, these gate replacements change both fusion architecture and temporal conditioning, so they do not isolate lag’s contribution. A reproducible NextItNet study should hold its backbone fixed and compare order-only, adjacent-gap, pairwise-interval, and shuffled/constant-time controls.

TiSASRec retains the latest L events and left-pads shorter histories; TLSRec uses session windows and repeated-session/item padding. Neither paper establishes missing-timestamp robustness. Suggested safeguards: explicit unknown-time masks, separate padding from genuine zero gaps, and derive normalization from observed history only—the released TiSASRec preprocessing computes scaling before splitting. Use request-time lag only when an actual request timestamp is supplied; never substitute the held-out target timestamp. If unavailable, omit lag or evaluate an explicitly labeled history-only proxy. [Author implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JiachengLi1995/TiSASRec/master/util.py).
